claims.reason: The proposed helper is `rw [← Associates.le_singleton_iff, Associates.prime_pow_dvd_iff_le (Associates.mk_ne_zero'.mpr hr) v.associates_irreducible]`. That is a thin wrapper that composes two existing API lemmas, which the rubric excludes. The repeated blocks are also not identical. In `intValuation_le_pow_iff_dvd` (lines 240–241) the rewrite is already the tail of a one-line `rw` chain, so the helper saves almost nothing. In `intValuation_exists_uniformizer` (lines 276–282) the hypotheses `mem` and `notMem` are first converted with `Ideal.dvd_span_singleton` and `Associates.mk_le_mk_iff_dvd`. Then `pow_one` and `Associates.mk_pow` are applied, and `hπ` comes from a separate nonzero proof. That proof stays at the Associates level and works with `¬ 2 ≤ count`, so it does not factor cleanly through a membership-form lemma. Only the three uses in `map_add_le_max'` (lines 141–156) are really alike. There the saving is mostly the trailing `exact v.associates_irreducible` side goals, which is cosmetic. No substantial mathematical argument is shared.

claims.reason: The two proofs `isNonarchimedean_intAdicAbvDef` and `isNonarchimedean_adicAbvDef` (lines 586–591 and 621–626) are literally the same apart from the valuation. Each unfolds the definition, takes `(toNNReal_strictMono hb).monotone`, rewrites `← h_mono.map_max`, and applies `map_add`. A generic lemma over `w : Valuation A ℤᵐ⁰` would be sound and cycle-free. The argument is only a routine four-line step that commutes a monotone map with `max`, so it is arguably a short calculation, which the rubric excludes. The proposed generic `AbsoluteValue` constructor is only sketched. The `eq_zero'` fields differ: the `R` version calls `intValuation_def` and the `K` version does not. The `intAdicAbv_*` and `adicAbv_coe_*` lemmas are already thin `rw` wrappers. So I cannot tell from the source whether the full refactor is worth it. The benefit is real but modest, as the candidate itself says. A generic statement would be `lemma isNonarchimedean_toNNReal_comp (hb : 1 < b) (w : Valuation A ℤᵐ⁰) : IsNonarchimedean (fun a => toNNReal (ne_zero_of_lt hb) (w a))`. Its proof would be the existing five lines with `w.map_add`.
